author: Declaration Desk
title: Bengal orders cinemas to restore prime-time shows for Bengali film, warns of licence action
dek: Halls had planned to drop 'Sadhak Bamakhyapa' for a Hindi release. The chief minister revived the 3 pm-9 pm Bengali-show rule and promised 51 new cinema halls.
body:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has directed cinema owners to restore prime-time screenings of the Bengali film Sadhak Bamakhyapa, which exhibitors had planned to cut back to make room for a new Hindi release, and warned that halls that do not show at least one Bengali film between 3 pm and 9 pm could lose their licences.

The direction came at a meeting with exhibitors, distributors and producers on Tuesday, according to reports. Mr Adhikari also said a committee would be set up by 30 November to examine the industry's problems, and that the state plans to build 51 cinema halls over the next year and a half.

## What happened

Sadhak Bamakhyapa released on 20 November. Some hall owners announced that they would withdraw it from 27 November to make space for Yeh Prem Mol Liya, a Hindi film produced by Rajshri Productions and distributed by Yash Raj Films that opens this Friday, according to reports. Exhibitors said they could not fit in enough shows for both, reports said. The film's makers said the move was disappointing given strong audiences, including houseful weekday shows.

After the meeting, the film's director, Sayantan Ghosal, said: "We are very happy. The chief minister has directed cinema hall owners to screen the movie," according to reports. A spokesperson for the production house SVF said Bengali cinema had "got a new life".

The requirement that halls screen at least one Bengali film in the 3 pm-9 pm window was introduced by the previous Trinamool Congress government, but industry representatives say enforcement had weakened, according to reports. Mr Adhikari said halls that refuse to comply could face action up to the cancellation of their licences. BJP MLA and actor Rudranil Ghosh said the intervention covered more than one film and applied to Bengali cinema in general, reports said.

## What else was announced

The review committee is expected to be headed by actor Mithun Chakraborty, with actor Prosenjit Chatterjee among its members, and will look at how screens are allocated and recommend remedies, according to reports. The government will also review complaints from producers, distributors and exhibitors about losses from cancelled or reduced shows; one report said police had been asked to survey those losses over three months.

The 51 new halls are to be built over about 18 months, with private investment invited, and the government has spoken of an ambition to raise the number of single-screen cinemas in the state to about 500, reports said. Many of the state's single-screen cinemas have closed in recent decades as audiences moved to multiplexes and streaming.

## Background

Bengali films have long struggled for screen time in their home state against Hindi and big South Indian releases, which bring larger audiences and higher ticket revenue for multiplexes. The prime-time rule is one of several measures states have used to protect regional cinema; Maharashtra has a similar requirement for Marathi films.

Exhibitors have not publicly responded to the licence warning. The government has not published a written order, and reports did not cite the legal provision behind the prime-time rule.
